P8.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor.
P8.bio: Hastie Lanyon is a doctor and colleague of Henry Jekyll, and an old friend of Mr. Utterson. He is cautious and suspicious of Jekyll's sanity. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind, and later refused to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him. After dining with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, he was shocked by his own decayed appearance and declared himself a doomed man who would never recover. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened his sealed envelope.

P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir.
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, colleague of Dr. Lanyon, and lawyer Utterson's acquaintance, known for charities and religion. He is hunted across the land as Carew's murderer. He swore never to set eyes on Hyde again, admitted Hyde dictated his will, and after Hyde vanished resumed his old friendships. He then shut his door against Utterson, vowed extreme seclusion, and spoke of an unnameable punishment. On the ninth of January he begged Lanyon to force open his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and receive a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeyed, and Jekyll confessed his moral turpitude with tears.

P22.tagline: Small man who comes at midnight in Jekyll's name.
P22.bio: The small man is a secret midnight visitor who comes in Dr. Jekyll's name to Dr. Lanyon's house. He is small, with a shocking facial expression. At midnight he knocked gently and crouched against the portico pillars; when Lanyon asked if he came from Dr. Jekyll, he gestured yes. He glanced back at a policeman and hurried inside. Lanyon then saw him clearly for the first time and was struck by his appearance. He is currently at Lanyon's house, having come secretly at midnight in Jekyll's name.

P10.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house.
P10.bio: Poole is the elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, obeyed by the housemaid, cook, and knife-boy, and directed by Mr. Utterson in the search. He is afraid and cannot bear it, with a white face and harsh broken voice. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, that Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, and that all servants had orders to obey Hyde. Later he reported Jekyll confined and silent, came to Utterson at night, and said he thought there had been foul play. He and Utterson broke in and found Hyde's body. He currently awaits Lanyon's arrival with a locksmith.
